title: Lithography and Patterning
description: How a pattern becomes a feature: resists, exposure, Rayleigh, DUV, multiple patterning, then EUV as a later light source — not the first word.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 6.152J
sourceReferences.notes: Photolithography as a unit process after the wafer exists.

sourceReferences.title: ASML lenses and mirrors
sourceReferences.notes: Rayleigh, NA, refractive DUV vs reflective EUV.

sourceReferences.title: ASML EUV systems
sourceReferences.notes: Source, mirrors, vacuum. High-NA is a later platform.

modules.title: Printing a layer
learningObjectives: Treat lithography as a stencil for later etch or implant
Walk coat, expose, and develop before naming a scanner

modules.title: What sets resolution
learningObjectives: Name wavelength, NA, and k1 as the three Rayleigh knobs
Treat focus and dose as a window, not a slogan

modules.title: DUV and tricks that extend it
learningObjectives: Identify 193 nm as the workhorse that still prints most layers
Explain why one exposure is split when Rayleigh says no

modules.title: EUV as a light source
learningObjectives: Treat EUV as a later light source after DUV, not the first word
Name mirrors, vacuum, and photon noise as the new physics

concepts.name: Photolithography
concepts.summary: Projecting patterns into resist to define features.
objectives: State photolithography as projecting a mask image into resist so later etch or implant has a stencil
Trace coat, expose, develop, and pattern transfer as the unit-process loop

concepts.name: Photoresists
concepts.summary: A film that changes solubility where the light hit.
objectives: Explain photoresist as a film whose solubility changes where light landed
Contrast a positive resist (exposed leaves) with a negative resist (exposed stays)

concepts.name: Masks and reticles
concepts.summary: The chrome (or multilayer) original the stepper reduces.
objectives: Describe a mask or reticle as the original the projection optic reduces onto the wafer
Explain why the wafer pattern is a reduced image of the reticle, not a contact print of chrome

concepts.name: Exposure and develop
concepts.summary: Dose as the thing you can miss in either direction.
objectives: Treat dose as a knob you can miss by underexposing or overexposing
Predict what happens to a feature when develop follows a wrong dose

concepts.name: Alignment marks
concepts.summary: How this layer finds the last one.
objectives: Explain alignment marks as how this layer finds the last one
Predict a miss when this layer is printed without locking to the previous marks

concepts.name: The Rayleigh criterion
concepts.summary: Resolution as k1 · λ / NA — three knobs, not one slogan.
objectives: State resolution as k1 · λ / NA and name what each symbol is
Predict the direction resolution moves when wavelength or NA changes

concepts.name: The k1 factor
concepts.summary: Process and illumination cleverness packed into a dimensionless number.
objectives: Treat k1 as process and illumination cleverness packed into a dimensionless number
Predict why shrinking k1 is not a free substitute for a shorter wavelength

concepts.name: The process window
concepts.summary: Focus and dose ranges that still print a legal CD.
objectives: Define the process window as the focus and dose ranges that still print a legal CD
Predict a CD miss when you leave the window in focus or in dose

concepts.name: Focus-exposure matrices
concepts.summary: The bossung plot as a lab object.
objectives: Describe a focus-exposure matrix as the lab object that maps the process window
Read a Bossung plot as CD versus focus at several doses

concepts.name: Line-edge roughness
concepts.summary: The wall is not a straight line.
objectives: Define line-edge roughness as the wall not being a straight line
Predict why a rough edge becomes a CD or device problem as features shrink

concepts.name: Deep ultraviolet lithography
concepts.summary: 248 and 193 nm as the workhorses that still print most layers.
objectives: Identify 248 nm and 193 nm as the workhorse wavelengths that still print most layers
Explain why DUV uses refractive lenses and why that path has a wavelength floor

concepts.name: Immersion lithography
concepts.summary: Water between lens and wafer to raise NA.
objectives: Explain putting water between lens and wafer as a way to raise NA
Predict the resolution gain and the new process risks water introduces

concepts.name: Optical proximity correction
concepts.summary: Distorting the mask so the wafer looks like the drawing.
objectives: Describe OPC as distorting the mask so the wafer looks like the drawing
Predict what an uncorrected dense feature does compared with an isolated one

concepts.name: Proximity and flare
concepts.summary: Neighbors and stray light changing the dose you thought you set.
objectives: Explain proximity and flare as neighbors and stray light changing the dose you thought you set
Diagnose a CD miss that tracks nearby pattern density rather than the scanner recipe

concepts.name: Multiple patterning
concepts.summary: Splitting one drawn layer across several litho-etch passes.
objectives: Explain multiple patterning as splitting one drawn layer across several litho-etch passes
Predict why a single 193 nm exposure cannot print a pitch the Rayleigh limit forbids

concepts.name: Pitch splitting
concepts.summary: Why a 20 nm pitch is not a 20 nm exposure.
objectives: State why a 20 nm pitch is not a 20 nm exposure
Trace a pitch-split sequence as two or more sparser exposures whose union is the drawn pitch

concepts.name: Overlay as a lithography budget
concepts.summary: Layer-to-layer error before anyone says EUV.
objectives: Define overlay as layer-to-layer placement error before anyone says EUV
Predict a via or contact fail when overlay eats the landing pad

concepts.name: EUV lithography
concepts.summary: 13.5 nm light, mirrors, and why refractive optics die.
objectives: Identify 13.5 nm as the light and mirrors as the optic because refractive materials absorb it
Contrast an EUV reflective path with a DUV refractive lens path

concepts.name: The EUV source
concepts.summary: A CO2 laser on tin droplets, tens of thousands of times a second.
objectives: Describe the source as a CO2 laser hitting tin droplets tens of thousands of times a second
Explain why source power is a throughput and dose budget, not a brochure number

concepts.name: Multilayer mirrors
concepts.summary: Bragg reflectors as the practical HVM projection optic at 13.5 nm.
objectives: Explain multilayer Bragg mirrors as the practical HVM projection optic once glass dies
Predict why each bounce costs photons and why the column is a chain of mirrors

concepts.name: Vacuum beam path
concepts.summary: Air eats EUV. The whole column is a chamber.
objectives: Explain why air absorbs EUV so the whole column is a vacuum chamber
Predict what a vented or leaking beam path does to the dose at the wafer

concepts.name: EUV pellicles
concepts.summary: A membrane that must protect the mask without eating the photons.
objectives: Describe an EUV pellicle as a membrane that must protect the mask without eating the photons
Predict the dose or throughput cost of a pellicle that is not optically free

concepts.name: Stochastic defects
concepts.summary: Photon and photoacid shot noise at EUV doses.
objectives: Explain stochastic defects as photon and photoacid shot noise at EUV doses
Predict why raising dose fights noise and spends throughput

concepts.name: Numerical aperture
concepts.summary: NA as a knob at EUV: resolution as 1/NA, depth of focus as ~1/NA².
objectives: State numerical aperture as the sine of the half-angle the optic can accept
Predict that raising NA buys resolution and spends depth of focus roughly as 1/NA²

concepts.name: Overlay
concepts.summary: Layer-to-layer alignment as a yield budget, not a slogan.
objectives: Treat overlay as a layer-to-layer yield budget, not a slogan
Diagnose an open or short as a tail of the overlay distribution eating the landing
